The first says the two firms need about $358B in combined annual revenue by 2029 to keep up with compute deals. 2029 has not arrived, so that part is not due. The second says any slowdown in growth would be fatal. This is conditional and has no date. By the evaluation date, neither firm had failed. Anthropic's S-1, as reported, shows quarterly revenue rising from about $4.7bn to $11.6bn to a reported $16.8bn. That means sequential growth fell from about 147% to about 45% while revenue still climbed fast. It is unclear whether this is the 'slowdown' he meant, so the condition is unknown. Under the rules, a conditional forecast with an unknown condition is not scored. Even if the condition were met, survival so far would not contradict an undated prediction of failure.

statement.excerpt: In any case, OpenAI and Anthropic need to make a combined $358 billion in annual revenue by 2029 to keep up with their $1.1 trillion in compute commitments. Any slowdown in their growth, as I discussed last week, would be fatal to two companies that have marketed themselves almost entirely by putting the cart before the horse.

from_speaker: need to make a combined $358 billion in annual revenue by 2029
to keep up with their $1.1 trillion in compute commitments
would be fatal to two companies
our_interpretation: The passage makes two commitments. (1) A necessity claim: unless the two companies together reach about $358B in annual revenue by 2029, they cannot keep up with their compute commitments. (2) A conditional forecast: if either company's revenue growth slows, that company will fail.
'By 2029' is read as annual revenue for calendar 2029. 'Keep up with' is read as paying compute obligations as they fall due without default, forced renegotiation, or rescue.

'Slowdown in their growth' is read as a real, sustained slowdown that takes a company off the path to the 2029 need. A lower percentage growth rate on a much larger base, with growth still very fast, does not clearly qualify.

'Fatal' is read as insolvency, bankruptcy, a distressed sale, or default on compute commitments. He gave no date for the failure, so a company surviving for a while after a slowdown does not contradict the forecast.
criteria.support_condition: After a documented, sustained slowdown in revenue growth, OpenAI or Anthropic becomes insolvent, files for bankruptcy, is sold in distress, or defaults on its compute commitments. Or the two companies' combined 2029 revenue falls well short of about $358B and they fail to meet their compute commitments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Combined calendar-2029 revenue falls well short of about $358B, yet both companies meet their compute commitments without default, forced renegotiation, or rescue. The undated 'fatal' part cannot be firmly contradicted by survival alone. At most it is weakened if both companies stay solvent through end-2029 after a clear, sustained slowdown.
